title: Zariski's lemma: a field of finite type over a field is a finite extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $K$ be a field together with a ring homomorphism $k\to K$ making $K$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra (a quotient of a polynomial ring $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$). Then $K$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, i.e. $K/k$ is a finite field extension.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem (theorem-nullstellensatz), tag 00FV, part (1) (for $K=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/\mathfrak m$, $\mathfrak m$ maximal); also Algebra, Lemma (lemma-silly-jacobson), tag 0CY7, with $R=k$ (a field is a Jacobson ring)
